01:26 Priya Rao: can we step back on encryption – for the dedicated flow we need KMS integration and customer-managed keys, also audit logs retained 13 months, is that doable?

02:08 Jordan Lee: we have SAML SSO and granular RBAC in console; we can set up an initial role mapping for your infra and ML teams.

02:34 Mike Thompson: yeah I can create a temporary role and rotate after the tests, i'll add that to the ticket.

03:02 Samir Patel: baseline hosted p95 was ~180ms per token for the prompt set, p99 was around 480ms on hosted, dedicated dropped p99 to ~220ms after batching and kv-warm. again these are approximate, i put raw traces in the spreadsheet.
03:22 Mike Thompson: hmmm, if we do private in region will we see further improvement? our users in eu-west need sub-200ms p99 for quick chat flows.
03:36 Samir Patel: likely yes, regional dedicated with smaller network hops + autoscaling tuned for steady QPS will improve tail latency, quantization helps too but watch quality tradeoffs.
03:49 Priya Rao: on quality tradeoffs, do you have regression tests and eval hooks? we need to ensure recall doesn't degrade with 4-bit.
04:01 Samir Patel: absolutely, Redwood Optimize has eval harnesses tied to prompt sets; we can run A/B tests and run regression alerts on your baseline prompts. if you give us a prioritized set Laura, we'll run that nightly.
04:16 Laura Gomez: will do, i'll share a 50 prompt priority list by end of week.

05:12 Laura Gomez: question on model variants: earlier you mentioned fallback to smaller models if capacity constrained, how seamless is that? we don't want weird quality jumps.
05:26 Avery Chen: the routing policy can be set to prefer primary model and only fallback to a compatible variant that we pre-validate against your eval-set; rollouts/gradual canary prevents surprises. we'll ensure compatibility tests are in the pilot's acceptance criteria.
05:41 Priya Rao: are logs scrubbed of PII before leaving our VPC for hosted runs? we need to make sure no PHI crosses.
05:56 Jordan Lee: it's configurable, we can set masking rules, or you can run inference in private so logs never leave your network. We'll include options and recommended patterns.
06:10 Laura Gomez: ok good. next, pricing – Avery, you mentioned a pilot credit and then usage rates. can you recap?
06:23 Avery Chen: yes, standard POC is 4 weeks with X credits included – we'll cover initial compute; after that usage-based pricing for hosted tokens and a reserved commit price for Dedicated. i'll send the updated pricing sheet with our recommended config for your QPS.
06:41 Mike Thompson: for Dedicated we need an estimate of throughput per machine to size -- how many queries per second at our 400 token average?
06:55 Samir Patel: for the quantized 4-bit model on 4x A100 with batching we saw roughly 120-150 req/s at 400 tokens if batching is tuned; the int8 dedicated runs were closer to 80-100 req/s but with slightly better quality. i'll add those numbers to the sheet with assumptions.

09:22 Priya Rao: any compliance concerns with quantized models? we just want to confirm there's no hidden state being retained beyond the expected KV cache.
09:34 Jordan Lee: KV cache is volatile per session, it doesn't persist across unrelated sessions unless you configure prefix caching; we'll document retention and purge policies.
09:46 Avery Chen: ok going to the bench results briefly – Samir, can you summarize the most surprising finding?
